newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- FOOTBALL SHARES TAKE A KICKING ON THE FOOTSIE

Shares in British football clubs have fallen 28 percent from their highs in the last two months, erasing a combined total of 1.1 billion stg from the market value of the quoted clubs. Soccer clubs have been the toast of the stock market over the past year, with a number of new flotations and at least five more flotations planned for the next two months. The slide in shares follows concern that prices have been overvalued and that forecasts of pay-per-view television revenues have been too optimistic.
-- WEAKER RETAIL DATA MAR TORIES' ECONOMIC HOPES

The latest retail survey of the Confederation of British Industry has revealed that growth in retail sales took an unexpected downturn in February, with consumers increasingly price-conscious. The decline, which followed a strong period of sales growth in the middle of last year, will come as a blow to government hopes of approaching the general election on the platform of a strong economic recovery.
-- GKN ORDERED TO PAY $600 MILLION RECORD DAMAGES BY US COURT

UK motor components and defence equipment group GKN has been ordered by a US court to pay almost $600 million (368 million stg) in compensation. The award, the largest commercial damages ever made against a UK company, comes after the company was found guilty of charges relating to the defrauding of franchisees of the group's specialist US exhaust retailer, Meineke Discount Mufflers. The award exceeds GKN's 'worst case scenario', which envisaged maximum damages of $554 million.
-- UK FAILS TO STIR EU ON 'MILLENNIUM BOMB'

Members of the European Union's Telecommunication Council responded with only lukewarm interest to warnings from UK science and technology minister Ian Taylor over the so-called 'millennium bomb' affecting computer chips. Experts have warned that chips, which may be in use in a range of applications from traffic light systems to hospital equipment, may not be able to cope with the millennium date change. Taylor has now raised the issue with the Council three times in the past year.
-- VAN MIERT THREAT TO RENAULT

Karel van Miert, the European competition commissioner, has indicated to the Belgian media that French car maker Renault is likely to face an uphill struggle to gain approval for state aid towards development of a factory in Spain. The Belgians are still furious at news that Renault is to close a profitable factory in northern Brussels. The European Commission has already concluded that Renault did not respect EU directives on worker consultation before announcing the Belgian closure.
-- PEUGEOT WORKERS IN STRIKE WARNING

Car workers at Peugeot's Coventry factory have threatened an all-out strike unless a dispute over pay and working hours is settled. The workers, who voted overwhelmingly for a strike in a ballot, have said they will start their action with a ban on overtime from next Friday, with strike action following the next week if no progress is made. Unions for the workers claim that Peugeot has refused to talk seriously about the issue of pay.
-- NEW CAR SALES GROWTH SLACKENS IN FEBRUARY

Figures out from the UK's Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders show that there were 162,887 new car registrations in February, an increase of 2.4 percent on the same month in 1996. However, the figures represent a considerable slackening from January's rapid growth, which saw new car registrations rise more than 9 percent year-on-year. The industry is particularly concerned about a lack of interest from private buyers.
-- GAS SUPPLIERS CALL FOR A THIRD TRIAL

Gas supply companies have called for a third test area for gas competition to be established later this year in order to maintain momentum towards full liberalisation of the domestic supply market next year. The call comes as the second test area, comprising some one million customers in the Sussex and Kent areas, begins its pilot project on Friday. TransCo, the BG subsidiary pipeline monopoly, has confirmed that 112,375 customers in the region - over 10 percent - have already decided to switch to one of the 14 companies competing to supply gas in the area.
-- C&W AND US WEST PLAN JOINT RUSSIAN OPERATION

UK telecommunications group Cable & Wireless is planning to merge its Russian operations with those of US regional operator US West in order to challenge the country's incumbent telecoms giants Rostelekom and Svyazinvest. C&W has a 32 percent stake in Russian long-distance operator PLD Telekom, while US West has 66.5 percent of wireless operator Russian Telecommunications Development Corp. News of the proposed deal comes as Moscow unveils plans to link Russia's two domestic companies, a move which prompted the World Bank to suspend its support for restructuring of the telecoms sector.
-- BSKYB, KIRCH END SATELLITE DEAL

Satellite television venture BSkyB has announced that it is to end a digital satellite joint venture agreement with German media group Kirch. The two groups cited 'failure to agree a number of fundamental issues' as the reason for the decision.
The Kirch alliance, which had been announced in July last year, was the second attempt by BSkyB to find a way in to the complex but potentially lucrative German pay TV market.
